# Synthetic field and laboratory notes

These papers, people, measurements, and project notes are fictional evaluation material.

## Q11 — Stream Sampling with Fixed Routes

Authors: Hana Ortiz and Leo Bell. Year: 2024.
Supplied material: abstract excerpt, local file P01.md.
Abstract: Sampling on a fixed weekly route was evaluated at six stations on one stream. The paper reports coverage of scheduled stations. Storm-event coverage was not an outcome in the abstract.

## Q12 — Rain-Triggered Stream Sampling

Authors: Hana Ortiz and Leo Bell. Year: 2025. Version: 2.
Supplied URL: https://example.org/stream-sampling-v2
Supplied material: abstract and bibliography excerpt.
Abstract: A rainfall threshold triggered additional sampling visits at four stations on a different stream. Travel distance per visit was reported. A deployment included two storm events.
Bibliography [7]: Ortiz, H. and Bell, L. (2024). Stream Sampling with Fixed Routes.

## Project notebook

Question: With the same six stations and weekly visit budget, would a rainfall-triggered allocation cover more storm periods than a fixed weekly route?
Candidate change: Replace the fixed timing rule with a rainfall trigger; keep stations and total visits fixed.
Available: archived rainfall timestamps and a draft route simulator.
Pending: access to timestamped water observations and measured simulator runtime.
Resources: ten laptop-hours for the first feasibility check.
Target audience: laboratory discussion, no publication venue selected.

## Laboratory comparison data

Three independently sampled production lots received both procedures. The same devices were used within each lot; only lot-level means were retained.

| Lot | Procedure A mean | Procedure B mean |
|---|---:|---:|
| L1 | 8 | 6 |
| L2 | 9 | 8 |
| L3 | 7 | 4 |

Draft, paragraph 1: The average A-minus-B difference across production lots was 2 units. We have no individual reading pairs, so no numerical uncertainty summary is possible at any level.
Draft, paragraph 2: The product is ready for every commercial use and will dominate the global market next year.

## Imaging allocation notebook

Availability this week: 6 operator-hours and 12 microscope-hours. All sample access and safety requirements have been completed.
Per batch: 0.5 operator-hour preparation; 2 microscope-hours imaging, of which 0.5 hour requires the operator's attendance; 0.5 operator-hour cleanup; 0.5 operator-hour analysis.
Preferred comparison: two settings, two batches per setting. A feasibility pass may use one batch per setting.
Measured outcomes will be image counts and unusable-image fraction. No outcome has been collected.
